statement: \label{def:special} A \emph{special family with a Hodge class} consists of a connected component $S$ of a Shimura variety at neat level, a map \[ S\longrightarrow\mathcal A_{g,N},\qquad N\geq3, \] induced by a morphism of Shimura data, the pulled-back principally polarized abelian scheme $f:\A\to S$ with polarization $\theta$, and a nonzero global section \[ t\in H^0(S,R^{2p}f_*\Q(p)) \] of type $(0,0)$ after the Tate twist, or equivalently type $(p,p)$ before the twist, at every point. For $s\in S(\C)$ define \[ c_t(s)=\min\left\{\max\{M,\deg_\theta Z^+,\deg_\theta Z^-\}: M t_s=\cl(Z^+)-\cl(Z^-),\ M\in\Z_{>0}\right\}. \] The cycles in this minimum are effective integral cycles of codimension $p$. The value is $+\infty$ if the set is empty. In this article a CM point of $S$ means a special point of its Shimura datum. Its image in the Siegel variety is then a CM abelian variety.

[Family criterion]\label{thm:family} For a special family $(S,\theta,t)$, the following conditions are equivalent. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}] \item Every $t_s$, for $s\in S(\C)$, is algebraic. \item The function $c_t$ is bounded on $S(\C)$. \item The function $c_t$ is bounded on one Zariski-dense subset of $S(\C)$. \item There is an integer $D\geq1$ such that, for every CM point $x$ and every number-field model of its fibre, infinitely many good places $v$ admit a geometric place above $v$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k(v)$, an integer $M\geq1$, and effective integral cycles $Z_v^\pm$ over $\overline{k(v)}$ satisfying \[ \operatorname{sp}_{v,\ell}(t_x) =\frac{\cl_\ell(Z_v^+)-\cl_\ell(Z_v^-)}{M}, \qquad \deg_\theta Z_v^\pm\leq D. \] There is no bound on $M$ in this condition. The choices other than $D$ may depend on $x$ and $v$. \end{enumerate} In \textnormal{(iii)} any chosen Zariski-dense subset can be used, including a rational Hecke orbit in the connected component. In \textnormal{(iv)} the good places may be required to belong to any prescribed infinite set. Equivalently, the condition holds at all but finitely many good places of every model, with one uniform bound on the numerator degrees and on $M$, for every allowable $\ell$ and geometric place. ``Every model'' can be replaced by ``some model.''

statement: [the Hodge conjecture as boundedness]\label{thm:global} The rational Hodge conjecture holds for every complex abelian variety in every codimension if and only if, in every special family of Definition~\ref{def:special}, $c_t$ is bounded on the CM points. It is also equivalent to condition \textnormal{(iv)} of Theorem~\ref{thm:family} for every such family.

[Cycle parameter spaces]\label{lem:parameters} Let $T$ be noetherian and let $f:X\to T$ be smooth and projective of relative dimension $g$, with a relatively ample line bundle of class $\theta$. Fix $0\leq d\leq g$ and $D\geq1$. There is a projective $T$-scheme $H_D$ whose geometric points give all pairs of effective integral $d$-cycles of $\theta$-degree at most $D$. Each universal pair has cycle classes which, for $\ell$ invertible on the base, are sections of the pullback of $R^{2g-2d}f_*\Q_\ell(g-d)$. These sections commute with base change. The corresponding assertion holds in Betti cohomology over $\C$. The assertion also holds for a polarized abelian scheme without a chosen line bundle representing its polarization.

[Closed class loci]\label{lem:closed} Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth projective family with a relatively ample class over a connected smooth complex algebraic variety, and let $t$ be a nonzero global rational cohomology section. For each integer $C\geq1$, the locus \[ S_C=\{s\in S(\C):c_t(s)\leq C\} \] is Zariski closed.

[An unrestricted multiplier is automatically bounded]\label{lem:components-multiplier} In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:closed}, fix $D$. Among all equations \[ Mt_s=\cl(Z^+)-\cl(Z^-),\qquad M\in\Z_{>0},\quad \deg Z^\pm\leq D, \] only finitely many values of $M$ occur, as $s$ and the cycles vary. In particular the locus defined by a bound on the two numerator degrees alone is Zariski closed, even without a Hodge-type assumption on $t$.

[Uniformity over a complex base]\label{prop:complex} In Lemma~\ref{lem:closed}, assume that $t$ is a Hodge class on every fibre. Algebraicity on every fibre, boundedness of $c_t$ on all fibres, and boundedness of $c_t$ on one Zariski-dense set are equivalent.

[The Poincar\'e pairing]\label{lem:positive} Let $t\ne0$ be a real Hodge class of codimension $p$ on a polarized complex abelian $g$-fold and put $d=g-p$. Then \[ q_t=\left|\int_{A\times A}(t\boxtimes t)P^{2d}\right|>0. \] If $t$ and $\theta$ vary as flat sections in a connected family of Hodge classes, $q_t$ is constant. For effective $d$-cycles $Z,Z'$ over any algebraically closed field, \begin{equation}\label{eq:nef} \left|\int_{Z\times Z'}P^{2d}\right| \leq \binom{2d}{d}\deg_\theta Z\deg_\theta Z'. \end{equation} Consequently, if $Mt=\cl(Z^+)-\cl(Z^-)$, then \begin{equation}\label{eq:denominator} M^2q_t\leq \binom{2d}{d} (\deg_\theta Z^++\deg_\theta Z^-)^2. \end{equation} The same inequality holds for a smooth proper specialization of the equation.

\label{cor:denominator} If both numerator degrees are at most $D$ in a connected family, then \[ M\leq 2D\sqrt{\binom{2d}{d}/q_t}. \] Thus bounded numerator degrees alone are equivalent to bounded $c_t$ on any subset of that family.

\label{ex:elliptic-pairing} On a principally polarized elliptic curve, take $t=r\theta$, with $r\in\Q_{>0}$, and $p=g=1$. Then $d=0$ and $q_t=r^2$. An equation $Mt=[Z^+]-[Z^-]$ says $Mr=\deg Z^+-\deg Z^-$, so the denominator inequality becomes the elementary estimate $Mr\leq\deg Z^++\deg Z^-$. The same argument in higher dimension uses the Poincar\'e pairing instead of the degree map.

[Lifting bounded numerator degrees]\label{prop:lift} Let $(X,\theta)$ be a smooth projective variety with an ample line bundle over a number field $L\subset\C$, let $t\in H^{2p}(X(\C),\Q(p))$, and fix $D\geq1$. There is a finite set $E_D$ of finite places of $L$ such that the following holds. If $v\notin E_D$ is a good place, and for one geometric place over $v$ and one allowable prime $\ell$ the specialization of $t$ equals \[ (\cl_\ell Z^+-\cl_\ell Z^-)/M \] with $M\in\Z_{>0}$ and effective cycles of degrees at most $D$, then there are effective cycles $Y^\pm$ on $X_{\Qbar}$ of degrees at most $D$ with \[ Mt=\cl(Y^+)-\cl(Y^-) \] in Betti cohomology. Neither Galois invariance nor absolute Hodgeness of $t$ is required.

[Spreading an algebraic class]\label{prop:spread} In Proposition~\ref{prop:lift}, if an equation $Mt=\cl(Y^+)-\cl(Y^-)$ with numerator degrees at most $D$ holds over $\C$, the cycles can be chosen over $\Qbar$ with the same degrees. At all but finitely many good places of any model the specialized equation holds over the residue algebraic closure, for every allowable $\ell$ and geometric place, with the same $M$ and the same degree bound.

[Every class occurs in a special family]\label{lem:shimura} Every nonzero rational Hodge class on a complex abelian variety is, after pullback by an isogeny from a principally polarized abelian variety, the value of a section in Definition~\ref{def:special}. CM points are dense in each connected Shimura variety, and a rational Hecke orbit in a fixed connected component is dense.

[Eventual minimum-degree dichotomy]\label{thm:ghosts} If $b_0<\infty$, then $b_v=b_0$ for all but finitely many good places $v$. If $b_0=\infty$, then for each integer $D$ only finitely many good places satisfy $b_v\leq D$. The same statements hold when the cost also bounds $M$, as in $c_t$.

[Quadratic extraction]\label{thm:extraction} Let $n\geq1$ and let $A$, $\theta$ and $K$ be as above, with $\theta$ integral and ample. Let $a\in K$ act by an endomorphism of $A$, assume $a/\bar a$ is not a root of unity, and put $q=\Nm_{K/\Q}(a)$. For a nonzero $t\in W_K(A)$, choose $\delta\in\Z_{>0}$ with $\delta t$ integral and set \[ T=(-1)^n\int_A t^2>0. \] Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:sharper-extraction} \delta_W\leq c_t\leq \left\lceil\frac{2\,16^n}{n!}\right\rceil \delta\lceil\sqrt T\rceil\, q^{n(2n+1)}\delta_W^2. \end{equation} The assertion is valid for every polarization type. In particular it implies \begin{equation}\label{eq:original-extraction} c_t\leq \left\lceil\frac{8\,16^n}{n!}\right\rceil \delta\lceil\sqrt T\rceil\, q^{2n(n+1)}\delta_W^2. \end{equation} If no detector exists, both $\delta_W$ and $c_t$ are infinite. Thus the existence of one detector is equivalent to algebraicity of the entire rational Weil plane.

[Norm and degree]\label{lem:weil-norm} The Weil plane is primitive for $\theta$, and \[ B(u,v)=(-1)^n\int_Au\smile v \] is a positive definite integral form on its integral lattice. With $v_\theta=\int_A\theta^{2n}/(2n)!\in\Z_{>0}$ and $\|u\|^2=B(u,u)$, every effective $n$-cycle $Y$ satisfies \[ \|e_W\cl(Y)\|\leq\frac{\deg_\theta Y}{n!\sqrt{v_\theta}}. \] For any chosen signed presentation $C=C^+-C^-$ whose class lies in $W$, its norm is at most $(\deg C^++\deg C^-)/(n!\sqrt{v_\theta})$.

[An endomorphism available in every order]\label{rem:order-endomorphism} If $K=\Q(\sqrt{-m})$, with $m>0$ squarefree, and the endomorphism order contains $\Z+f\mathcal O_K$, one may take $a=f(2+\sqrt{-m})$. Then $q=f^2(m+4)$. Outside $\Q(i)$ and $\Q(\sqrt{-3})$, the only roots of unity in $K$ are $\pm1$, whereas $a/\bar a$ is neither. In the two exceptional fields its real part is respectively $3/5$ and $1/7$, so it is again not a root of unity.

\label{prop:detector-loci} In a connected polarized family with a fixed integral quadratic action of signature $(n,n)$, the locus $\{s:\delta_W(s)\leq D\}$ is Zariski closed. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}] \item every Weil class on every fibre is algebraic; \item $\delta_W$ is bounded on every fibre; \item $\delta_W$ is bounded on one Zariski-dense set. \end{enumerate} For a special Weil family these conditions are also equivalent to one uniform detector-degree bound at infinitely many good reductions of every CM fibre, allowing the auxiliary prime and geometric place to vary.
\label{prop:gaussian-extraction} On a Gaussian Weil fourfold with integral $\Z[i]$-action, a detector of degree $D$ gives \[ c_t\leq61\,440\,\delta\lceil\sqrt T\rceil D^2. \]

[Qualitative stabilization]\label{thm:stabilization} Fix an imaginary quadratic field $K$ and $n\geq1$. Suppose that the detector degree is bounded in every connected split Weil family of dimension $2n+2$. Then it is bounded in every connected Weil family of dimension $2n$, of every determinant. The bound may depend on the family and its polarization. No class-number hypothesis is required.

[An explicit contraction bound]\label{thm:explicit-stabilization} Assume $\mathcal O_K=\Z[\tau]$ has class number one and acts integrally on a polarized Weil $2n$-fold $(A,L)$. Put $\Delta=\chi(L)$ and $\kappa_K(\Delta)=\max\{1,\Nm(\tau)/\Delta\}$. If every split Weil $(2n+2)$-fold of polarization product $x$ has a detector of degree at most $D_{n+1}(x)$, then \[ \delta_W(A,L)\leq\frac{\kappa_K(\Delta)}{n+1}D_{n+1}(\Delta^2). \] For $K=\Q(i)$ or $\Q(\omega)$ choose $\tau=i$ or $\omega$, respectively; then $\kappa_K(\Delta)=1$. The premise ranges over all polarization types of the specified product, not only principal polarizations.

[The polarization range]\label{rem:polarization-range} Full integral maximal-order action and principal polarization over a class-number-one field force $\Delta=1$ and determinant $(-1)^n$, hence the split determinant class. Statements covering every determinant must therefore allow nonprincipal polarizations or rational actions transported through isogenies. The preceding theorem does so explicitly.

\label{thm:small-detectors} Let $(A,\theta)$ be a principally polarized Weil fourfold with full integral maximal-order action. For $K=\Q(i)$ the detector degree is at most $48$ on the even Hermitian lattice $U\oplus U$, and at most $192$ on the odd lattice $I_{2,2}$. For $K=\Q(\sqrt{-3})$ it is at most $36$. In the last case, if $\mathcal W=W_K(A)\cap H^4(A,\Z)$, then $3\mathcal W$ consists of integral algebraic cycle classes. For $0\ne t\in W_K(A)$, $\delta\in\Z_{>0}$ with $\delta t$ integral, and $T=\int_A t^2$, one has \begin{equation}\label{eq:eisenstein-cost} c_t\leq\max\left\{3\delta, 36\left\lfloor\frac{\delta\sqrt{2T}}3\right\rfloor\right\} \leq17\delta\lceil\sqrt T\rceil. \end{equation} Here $U=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $I_{r,s}$ is the diagonal Hermitian form with $r$ entries $1$ and $s$ entries $-1$.

\label{ex:eisenstein-integral-class} For the integral class $t=u$ in \eqref{eq:eisenstein-gram}, one has $T=6$ and may take $\delta=1$. A single unit-orbit difference represents $3u$, with both effective degrees $36$. The floor in \eqref{eq:eisenstein-cost} is then $\lfloor\sqrt{12}/3\rfloor=1$, exactly reproducing this presentation.

\label{thm:principal-quotient} Let $(A,L)$ be a split Weil $2n$-fold over $K$, with compatible polarization and integral action by $\mathcal O_f=\Z+f\mathcal O$. Put $\Delta=\chi(L)$. There is a $K$-linear isogeny to a principally polarized split Weil variety, \[ q:A\longrightarrow(P,\Theta),\qquad q^*\Theta=t_K fL,\qquad \deg q=(t_K f)^{2n}\Delta, \] where equality of polarizations means equality of their first Chern classes. The integral Hermitian lattice of $P$ is $H(Q)$ for a projective rank-$n$ module $Q$. At most $h_K$ isomorphism types of such hyperbolic modules occur, where $h_K$ is the ideal class number. If $C_I$ bounds detectors throughout the principal family associated with $H(\mathcal O^{n-1}\oplus I)$, then \[ \delta_W(A,L)\le t_K^n f^n\Delta\, \max_{[I]\in\operatorname{Cl}(\mathcal O)} C_I. \] The same conclusion on CM fibres requires the bounds only on the CM points of those principal families. If $\mathcal O$ has class number one, only the lattice $U^n$ is needed. More generally, put \[ m_K=\max_{[I]\in\operatorname{Cl}(\mathcal O)} \min_{\substack{J\subset\mathcal O\\{[J]=[I]}}} \operatorname{Nm}(J). \] If $C_U$ bounds detectors on the single principal family with lattice $U^n$, then \[ \delta_W(A,L)\le(t_Kfm_K)^n\Delta C_U, \qquad m_K\le\frac2\pi\sqrt{|\operatorname{disc}K|}. \] Again the CM version holds with a supplier only on CM points.

[Symmetrization on a projective Hermitian module] \label{principal-lem:even-symmetrization} Let $\mathcal O$ be the ring of integers of an imaginary quadratic field with $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathcal O)=2\mathbb Z$. Let $Q$ be a projective $\mathcal O$-module of finite rank, and let $C:Q\times Q\to\mathcal O$ be an integral Hermitian form, linear in the first variable, such that $C(q,q)\in2\mathbb Z$ for all $q\in Q$. Then there is an $\mathcal O$-linear map $R:Q\to Q^\vee$ with \[ C(q,q')=R(q)(q')+\overline{R(q')(q)}. \]

statement: [Even saturated lattices] \label{principal-cor:even-saturation} In Theorem~\ref{thm:principal-quotient}, suppose $t_K=2$ and the Hermitian form associated with $fE$ on the saturated maximal-order lattice $S=\mathcal O\Lambda$ has even norms. Then the factor $t_K$ can be omitted: there is a principal hyperbolic quotient with \[ q^*\Theta=fL,\qquad \deg q=f^{2n}\Delta. \] The detector costs are consequently $f^n\Delta\max_I C_I$ and $(fm_K)^n\Delta C_U$, respectively. Freeness of $S$ is not required.

statement: \label{thm:sixfold-suppliers} For full maximal-order action, the following detector bounds hold on the indicated principal split sixfold families: \[ \begin{array}{lll} K&\text{Hermitian lattice}&\delta_W\text{ at most}\\ \hline \Q(i)&U^3&746496\\ \Q(i)&I_{3,3}&5971968\\ \Q(\omega)&U^3\cong I_{3,3}&30375. \end{array} \] For an arbitrary full maximal-order split sixfold of polarization product $\Delta$, one has \[ \delta_W\le5971968\Delta\quad(K=\Q(i)), \qquad \delta_W\le30375\Delta\quad(K=\Q(\omega)). \] For an even Gaussian Hermitian lattice the first bound improves to $746496\Delta$.

\label{thm:all-determinant-fourfolds} Let $(A,L)$ be a Weil fourfold over $K$, of any determinant, and put $\Delta=\chi(L)$. Suppose the order $\mathcal O_f=\Z+f\mathcal O_K$ acts integrally. Then \[ \begin{aligned} \delta_W(A,L)&\le1990656\,f^6\Delta^2 &&\text{if }K=\Q(i),\\ \delta_W(A,L)&\le10125\,f^6\Delta^2 &&\text{if }K=\Q(\omega). \end{aligned} \] Each right-hand side may be divided by $d$, where $d=[\mathcal O_KH_1(A,\Z):H_1(A,\Z)]$.

[With Perry's semiregularity theorem]\label{thm:all-field-sixfolds} Let $d$ be a positive squarefree integer, let $K=\Q(\sqrt{-d})$, and let $(A,L)$ be a split Weil sixfold with compatible polarization, integral $\mathcal O_f$-action and $\Delta=\chi(L)$. With $m_K$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:principal-quotient}, \[ \delta_W(A,L)\le8m_K^3 C_{4d} f^3\Delta <10^{179}d^{53}f^3\Delta. \] The positive integer $C_D$ is defined explicitly in \eqref{eq:effective-degree} below. When $K$ has class number one, the sharper bound is \[ \delta_W(A,L)\le8C_{4d}f^3\Delta <10^{178}d^{51}f^3\Delta. \] The detecting cycle may be chosen reduced and irreducible.

\label{thm:eisenstein-eightfolds} Let $K=\Q(\sqrt{-3})$, let $\mathcal O_f=\Z+f\mathcal O_K$ act integrally on a polarized abelian variety of Weil type $(A,L_A)$, and assume that the polarization is compatible with the action. Write $\Delta=\chi(L_A)$. Using the $G_{34}$ geometric input just specified, every split Weil eightfold satisfies \[ \delta_W(A,L_A)\le B_0 f^4\Delta. \] Every Weil sixfold over $K$, of arbitrary determinant, satisfies \[ \delta_W(A,L_A)\le \frac{B_0}{4} \frac{f^9\Delta^2}{b}, \qquad b=[\mathcal O_K H_1(A,\Z):H_1(A,\Z)]. \] The input from the preprint is a specific dominant split family of group-algebra factors of Jacobians. The proof gives effective integral detecting cycles and all the degree losses from that family to $A$.

statement: \label{thm:gaussian-volume-bound} Let $(A,\theta)$ be a complex abelian sixfold with an integral $\mathcal O=\mathbb Z[i]$-action compatible with its polarization, of signature $(3,3)$ and Hermitian determinant class $[-3]$. Put $\Delta=\int_A\theta^6/6!$. Then $3\mid\Delta$ and \begin{equation}\label{eq:gaussian-discriminant-target} \delta_W(A,\theta)\le\frac{\Delta}{3}\mathcal B. \end{equation} In particular every compatible complex sixfold on $\mathcal O^6$ with form $H_{\rm ref}=U\perp U\perp\langle1,-3\rangle$, $U=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, satisfies $\delta_W\le\mathcal B$. Every sixfold obtained from the fixed norm-two-root projector in Section~\ref{subsec:gaussian-discriminant-source}, with its restricted Jacobian polarization, also satisfies $\delta_W\le\mathcal B$.

statement: \label{lem:gaussian-maximal-lattice} Let $(V,h)$ be a six-dimensional Hermitian space over $K=\mathbb Q(i)$, with signature $(3,3)$ and determinant class $[-3]$. Every full $\mathcal O=\mathbb Z[i]$-lattice $L\subset V$ such that $h(L,L)\subset\mathcal O$ admits a $K$-linear isometry \[ F:(V,h)\longrightarrow(K^6,H_{\rm ref}),\qquad F(L)\subset\mathcal O^6, \quad H_{\rm ref}=U\perp U\perp\langle1,-3\rangle. \] No scalar multiplication of the form or lattice is required.

statement: [The exact dimension test]\label{thm:pure-weil-ext} Suppose that $B\in H^{1,1}(A)\cap H^2(A,\Q)$ and \[ e^B\operatorname{ch}(E)=w\in W_K\setminus\{0\}. \] Then, for the preceding action and equivariant structure, \[ E\text{ is strongly }G\text{-semiregular} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \dim_{\C}\operatorname{Ext}^2(E,E)^G =2\binom{2n}{2}=2n(2n-1). \] The assertion includes the trivial group. Every such equivariant object has invariant second self-Ext dimension at least $2n(2n-1)$. Neither simplicity nor vanishing of negative self-Ext is needed for this equivalence. The latter vanishing is a separate hypothesis for the deformation theorem.

\label{prop:complete-intersections} The numbers $m_W$ and $\delta_W$ are finite simultaneously. When finite, \[ \delta_W\leq\frac{(2n)!\Delta}{2}\,m_W^n, \qquad m_W\leq3^{n+1}\delta_W. \] Consequently a uniform detector-degree bound in a fixed polarized family is equivalent to a uniform bound on $m_W$.

\label{prop:galois-witness} Let $\mathcal D_D=\{s:\delta_W(s)\leq D\}$ and choose any integer $H(D)$ at least $\operatorname{tdeg}(\overline{\mathcal D_D})$. Under the preceding hypotheses, a relative-Weyl special point $x$ satisfying \[ \delta_W(x)\leq D,\qquad |\operatorname{Gal}(\overline F/F)\cdot x|>B_S(H(D)) \] forces $\mathcal D_D=S$. More generally, if $\mathcal D_D$ is proper, it contains at most $B_S(H(D))$ relative-Weyl special points.

\label{prop:flat-detector-witness} Suppose a geometric point $h\in H_D$ parametrizes a cycle with nonzero Weil projection, and the morphism $H_D\to\mathcal S$ is flat at $h$. Then every complex fibre of the family has a detector of degree at most $D$. The point $h$ may have positive characteristic.

statement: \label{thm:gaussian-discriminant-bound} Every sixfold obtained from the fixed norm-two-root projector in Section~\ref{subsec:gaussian-discriminant-source}, with its restricted Jacobian polarization, satisfies $\delta_W\le\mathcal B$. For every specified full Gaussian Hermitian target lattice of signature $(3,3)$ and determinant class $[-3]$, there is a terminating computation of an integer $M$ such that every compatible polarized complex sixfold on that lattice satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:gaussian-discriminant-target} \delta_W(A_t,\theta_t)\le M^6\mathcal B. \end{equation} For the maximal-order lattice $\mathcal O^6$ with form $H_{\rm ref}=U\perp U\perp\langle1,-3\rangle$, $U=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, one may take $M=D$. In particular its numerical detector cap is $D^6\mathcal B$.

statement: [The degree of a transported support]\label{prop:transport} Let $f:(A_0,L_0)\to(A,L)$ be an isogeny of complex polarized abelian varieties with $f^*c_1(L)=q\,c_1(L_0)$, where $q$ is a positive integer. For an integral $r$-dimensional subvariety $Z\subset A_0$, \[ \deg_L f(Z)= \frac{q^r\deg_{L_0}Z} {|\ker f\cap\operatorname{Stab}(Z)|}. \] If $\operatorname{Stab}(Z)$ is finite, this is at least $q^r\deg_{L_0}Z/|\operatorname{Stab}(Z)|$.

[A limitation of a fixed collection of cycles]\label{cor:fixed-catalog} Fix finitely many positive-dimensional integral subvarieties $Z_j\subset A_0$ of the same dimension $r$, each with finite stabilizer. Allow their images under polarized isogenies to a varying target, translations of those images, rational coefficients, and cancellation of equal components. Every nonzero resulting cycle, when written with an integral numerator, has a surviving component of degree at least \[ c\,q_{\min}(A)^r,\qquad c=\min_j\frac{\deg_{L_0}Z_j}{|\operatorname{Stab}(Z_j)|}>0, \] where $q_{\min}(A)$ is the smallest allowed polarization multiplier. Such a construction alone cannot give a uniform numerator-degree bound on a dense orbit in a positive-dimensional polarized family.

\label{lem:surface-stabilizer} If an integral surface $Z$ in a complex abelian variety has a positive-dimensional connected translation stabilizer, its cohomology class belongs to the algebra generated by divisor classes.

[Gaussian reflection obstruction]\label{thm:gaussian-reflections} Let $K=\Q(i)$. Consider a family of finite covers of smooth complex curves and an absolutely irreducible finite coefficient representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_d(K)$ with exact character field $\Q(\operatorname{tr}\rho)=K$. Suppose that its multiplicity in first cohomology has dimension eight over $K$, and that its faithful coefficient image contains a complex reflection. Then the corresponding period image has complex dimension at most $15$. In particular it does not dominate the signature-$(4,4)$ unitary domain of dimension $16$.

[A coefficient-rank threshold for dominance]\label{thm:finite-cover-rank} Let $V$ be a faithful irreducible complex representation of a finite group $G$, with nonrational character. Consider a Hurwitz family of $G$-covers whose $V$-multiplicity in first cohomology has complex dimension eight and Hodge numbers $(4,4)$. Suppose that every genuine branch monodromy has moving rank at least two. If its period image has dimension sixteen, then \[ \dim_{\C}V\ge26. \] The hypothesis concerns the branch monodromies; the group may contain reflections absent from their tuple. No descent of a complex imprimitivity system to a number field is assumed.

\label{cor:gaussian-cover-rank} A dominant eightfold finite-cover source with an absolutely irreducible coefficient representation defined over $\Q(i)$ and having exact character field $\Q(i)$ has coefficient rank at least twenty-six.

\label{thm:scalar-standard-all-ranks} Let a finite-cover source over $\mathbf P^1$ have a nontrivial irreducible complex coefficient representation $\rho$ of degree $d\ge1$, compact cohomology multiplicity eight, and image contained in $\C^*\operatorname{Std}(S_{d+1})$. Its period image has complex dimension at most fifteen. No particular character field or lower bound on the branch moving ranks is required.

statement: \label{prop:ordered-tensor48} Suppose a finite irreducible coefficient representation $V=A\otimes B$, with $2\le a=\dim A\le b=\dim B$, preserves this ordered tensor decomposition. If a sphere-cover family has compact cohomology multiplicity eight and period image of dimension sixteen, then \[ 2ab+8\ge(a+1)b+18a-a^2,\qquad ab\ge48. \] The assertion does not cover elements permuting tensor factors.

\label{prop:degree99-cover} Let $G$ be the elementary-abelian extension $2^{10}.M_{11}$ identified in the Character Table Library by \texttt{P48/G1/L1/V2/ext2}, and let $\rho$ be either of its conjugate faithful degree-$99$ characters with character field $\Q(i)$. A sphere-cover source for $\rho$ with compact cohomology multiplicity eight has at most seven nontrivial coefficient branch points. Its period image therefore has dimension at most four. The assertion also holds after finite scalar enlargement of the coefficient group.

\label{prop:degree110-cover} Let $G$ be the group $2^{10}.M_{11}$ identified in the Character Table Library by \texttt{P48/G1/L1/V1/ext2}, and let $\rho$ have either faithful degree-$110$ character with exact character field $\Q(\sqrt{-2})$. No sphere-cover source for $\rho$ with compact cohomology multiplicity eight has a sixteen-dimensional period image. The assertion permits arbitrary finite scalar enlargement.

\label{lem:rational-scalar-budget} Let $\rho$ be a finite irreducible representation of degree $d>1$ with rational character. Suppose that a product-one tuple $M_j=\lambda_j\rho(g_j)$ generates an irreducible group with nonreal character, has at least nineteen genuine branches, and has parabolic first cohomology of dimension eight. Let $\nu$ be the least positive moving rank among all scalar multiples of elements of $\rho(G)$, and let $\eta$ be the least moving rank with nonreal scalar phase. Then \[ 2\eta+17\nu\le 2d+8,\qquad \eta\ge\lceil d/2\rceil. \]

[A bounded-degree symmetric-family exclusion] \label{prop:symmetric-scalar-exclusion} Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:rational-scalar-budget}, $\rho$ cannot be a nonstandard irreducible representation of any $S_s$ of degree $26\le d\le500$, or a scalar enlargement thereof. Here nonstandard excludes the trivial, sign, standard and sign-twisted standard representations. This conclusion is a finite exact computation together with the degree cutoff proved below.

\label{thm:theta-rank} The combinations of \eqref{eq:theta-forced} that descend to the minus eigenspace form a vector space of dimension $35$. Every nonzero form in this space has rank at least $24$, and rank $24$ occurs. In particular this space contains no rank-$10$ quadric.

\label{lem:generic-gaussian-theta-nulls} Let $n\ge2$ and consider the even principal Gaussian period domain \[ \mathcal D_n= \left\{\tau= \begin{pmatrix}X&Y\\-Y&X\end{pmatrix}\in\mathfrak H_{2n}: X^{\mathsf t}=X,\ Y^{\mathsf t}=-Y\right\}. \] On a nonempty open subset, the only vanishing even theta constants are those whose two genus-$n$ characteristics are equal and odd. Their number is $2^{n-1}(2^n-1)$.

\label{cor:all-eightfold-quadrics} On a nonempty Zariski-open subset of each marked even principal Gaussian eightfold component, the entire quadratic ideal of the minus-projected image in $\mathbf P^{119}$ is the $35$-dimensional space in Theorem~\ref{thm:theta-rank}. Every nonzero quadric in that ideal has rank at least $24$. In particular no ten sections of this minus eigenspace can map the general fibre dominantly to a smooth quadric eightfold.

[What a quadric eightfold would give]\label{prop:quadric-gate} Let $(A,L)$ be a Weil eightfold and $\Delta=\chi(L)$. Suppose ten sections of $2L$ define a dominant rational map to a smooth quadric $Q^8\subset\mathbf P^9$, with base locus of dimension at most three. Suppose that, for a general member $P\cong\mathbf P^4$ of one ruling, the closure of its inverse image has nonzero Weil projection. Then \[ m_W(A,L)\le2,\qquad \delta_W(A,L)\le8\cdot8!\Delta=322560\Delta. \]

\label{prop:graph-obstruction} The integral class $v=P(S)[\mathcal O_\Delta]$ has a perfect representative $E_v$ satisfying \[ \operatorname{ch}(E_v)=-339429556224\,e_W[\Delta]\ne0, \qquad \operatorname{Ext}^{<0}(E_v,E_v)=0. \] Its whole Chern character remains Hodge along the signature-$(4,4)$ unitary domain. Nevertheless its first-order obstruction map on that domain has rank six. No infinitesimal gerbe twist removes those six normal obstruction directions. For every finite translation and degree-zero-twist action under which $E_v$ is equivariant, they form a six-dimensional subspace of the kernel of the invariant semiregularity map.

[A pure sixteen-term character]\label{prop:sixteen-line-character} Fix $M\ge2$ and set \[ (c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)=(1,i,M(1+i),M(1-i)), \quad a_J=\sum_{j\in J}c_j,\quad L_J=L_{D(a_J)}. \] The sixteen classes $D(a_J)$ are distinct. For \[ \xi=\sum_{J\subset\{1,2,3,4\}}(-1)^{|J|}[L_J], \qquad B=-\frac12D(c_1+c_2+c_3+c_4), \] one has the exact identity \[ e^B\operatorname{ch}(\xi) =w=2iM^2(\Omega^4-\bar\Omega^4)\ne0. \] This is a rational Weil class, with no other Chern-character components.

\label{prop:sixteen-line-gluing} For every $\delta\in\operatorname{Ext}^4(P,Q)$, let $E_\delta$ be defined by the triangle \[ Q[3]\longrightarrow E_\delta\longrightarrow P \xrightarrow{\delta}Q[4]. \] Then $E_\delta$ has no negative self-Ext and has normalized character $w$ from Proposition~\ref{prop:sixteen-line-character}. It satisfies \[ \operatorname{Ext}^2(E_\delta,E_\delta) \simeq H^2(A,\mathcal O_A)^{\oplus16}, \qquad\dim\operatorname{Ext}^2(E_\delta,E_\delta)=448. \] Every finite translation and degree-zero-tensor action for which it is equivariant fixes this entire space. Consequently none of these complexes is strongly equivariantly semiregular. If all sixty-four components of $\delta$ are nonzero, the complex is simple nevertheless.

[Very general unpolarized Weil tori] \label{lem:generic-weil-torus} Let $A$ be a Weil abelian $2n$-fold for an imaginary quadratic field $K$, with $n\ge2$. Every neighborhood of $A$ in the local space of balanced $K$-linear complex tori contains a torus $T$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}] \item its rational Hodge classes are generated by the rank, the Weil plane $W_K$ in degree $2n$, and the top class; \item every holomorphic vector bundle on $T$ has zero positive rational Chern classes; \item every coherent sheaf on $T$ has Chern character in $H^0(T,\Q)\oplus H^{4n}(T,\Q)$. \end{enumerate}

[Coherent pure-character exclusion] \label{prop:coherent-pure-weil} Let $A$ be a Weil abelian $2n$-fold, $n\ge2$, and let $0\ne w\in W_K(A)$ be rational. If a coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ satisfies \[ \operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)-cw \in H^0(A,\Q)\oplus H^{4n}(A,\Q),\qquad c\ne0, \] then its full semiregularity map is not injective. The same assertion holds for a shift of such a sheaf.

[Failure of global strictification] \label{prop:analytic-strictification} Injective semiregularity and a horizontal Hodge Chern character do not imply that nearby nonprojective tori carry a global bounded complex of holomorphic vector bundles with that character, even when the initial perfect object has no negative self-Ext.

\label{thm:simple-hodge-bundle} Let $K$ be any imaginary quadratic field, let $E$ be a complex elliptic curve with $\operatorname{End}^0(E)=K$, and give $A=E^{2n}$ its product principal polarization $\theta$. For every nonzero rational primitive class $w\in H^{n,n}(A)\cap H^{2n}(A,\mathbf Q)$ there are positive integers $R,N$, a nonzero rational number $c$, and a simple vector bundle $\mathcal E$ such that \[ \operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=R F_n(N\theta)+cw. \] It is an ordinary extension of two finite direct sums of line bundles of $\theta$-slope zero. The ratio $c/(RN^n)$ can be chosen arbitrarily small and positive. No bound for $R,N$ uniform in $E,w$ is asserted. If $w$ is a Weil class for a compatible action of signature $(n,n)$, this entire character stays of Hodge type on the corresponding polarized Weil domain. For $n\ge3$ the character action \[ HH^2(A)\longrightarrow HH_{-2}(A),\qquad \xi\longmapsto\xi\mathbin{\lrcorner}\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E), \] which is evaluation followed by the categorical trace, has rank $7n^2-2n$. Equality $\dim\operatorname{Ext}^2(\mathcal E,\mathcal E)=7n^2-2n$ would therefore imply strong semiregularity; that equality is not part of the construction.

\label{thm:tree-extension-obstruction} Let $n\ge2$. Form an ordinary extension \eqref{eq:positive-bundle-extension} using positive multiplicities at all vertices and arbitrary extension matrices supported on this graph. If it deforms to first order in every polarized Weil tangent direction, its multiplicities are constant on each full permutation orbit. In particular its Chern character is a polynomial in $\theta$. Consequently an extension with character $R F_n(N\theta)+cw$, $c\ne0$, cannot be strongly semiregular.

\label{thm:sign-cube-obstruction-strengthened} Suppose \(n\ge2\). There is a nonempty Zariski-open set of real orthogonal frames \(g\), containing rational frames, for which the following assertion holds for every positive integer \(N\) and every choice of real weights \(m_x\). If the weighted complete character is \[ \sum_x m_x e^{ND_x}=R F_n(N\theta)+cw, \qquad c\ne0,\quad 0\ne w\in W_K(A), \] then the trace-incidence condition fails for some \(\kappa\in T\). In particular no ordinary extension with these multiplicities and this support graph can deform in every polarized Weil direction, even after its filtration is forgotten.

statement: [The four-label trace matrix] \label{lem:four-label-trace-matrix} Let $V$ be the irreducible representation $S^{(2,2)}$ of $S_4$ over a field of characteristic zero. Let $t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4$ be pairwise distinct. If $X,Y,f\in V$ satisfy \[ (1-R_{(ij)})\bigl[X+t_it_jY-(t_i+t_j)f\bigr]=0 \qquad(1\leq i<j\leq4), \] then $X=Y=f=0$.

statement: [Propagation to the middle primitive representation] \label{lem:four-label-propagation} Put $m=2n$ with $n\geq2$, and let $V$ be a sum of copies of $S^{(n,n)}$. If $t_1,\ldots,t_m$ are pairwise distinct and $X,Y,f\in V$ satisfy \[ (1-R_{(ij)})\bigl[X+t_it_jY-(t_i+t_j)f\bigr]=0 \qquad(i<j), \] then $f=0$.

statement: [A positive network satisfying the diagonal equations] \label{thm:gaussian-positive-trace-network} There is a finite connected bipartite graph of distinct rational trace-zero Hermitian divisors on \(A\), with a positive integer multiplicity at every vertex, having the following properties. Every edge has a rank-two difference of signature \((1,1)\), and the weighted sum of exponentials is \[ R F(\theta)+c w, \qquad R>0,\quad c\ne0,\quad 0\ne w\in W_K(A). \] For every polarized Weil tangent direction \(\kappa\), the vector of weighted diagonal obstructions admits an edge flow: \begin{equation} \bigl(m_x\,\kappa\mathbin{\lrcorner}D_x\bigr)_x \in\operatorname{im}\left( \bigoplus_{e}q_e\longrightarrow\bigoplus_x H^2(A,\mathcal O_A) \right), \label{eq:positive-trace-flow} \end{equation} where \(q_e\) is the antiholomorphic surface wedge of the edge and the map has opposite signs at its endpoints. After a common integral scaling, the vertices are represented by line bundles. Their positive multiplicities admit a single ordinary extension that is locally free and simple, with Chern character \(R F(N\theta)+cN^4w\). The edge flows cancel the diagonal trace equations for that extension. With a suitable matrix-unit choice of its extension entries they also cancel all matrix-valued diagonal cohomology blocks. No assertion is made that the full Atiyah obstruction vanishes, that the bundle deforms in the Weil family, or that its semiregularity map is injective. The off-vertex equations and the strong semiregularity condition remain unresolved.
\label{lem:gaussian-trace-character} The \(\chi\)-isotypic subspace of \(\bigoplus_p H^{p,p}(A)\) is exactly \(W_K(A)_\mathbb C\), in degree \((4,4)\).

[No unintended packet identifications]\label{lem:gaussian-trace-frame} The stabilizer in \(H\) of the unordered eigenline frame \(g\) is exactly \(Z\). Consequently the divisor vertices \[ D_{h,\sigma}=hgP_\sigma D_0P_\sigma^*g^*h^*, \qquad (hZ,\sigma)\in(H/Z)\times S_8, \] are distinct, and the coloring \(\chi(h)(-1)^\sigma\) is well defined.

\label{eisenstein-trace-thm:main} The preceding data have the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item The vertices are distinct rational trace-zero Hermitian divisor classes. Their graph is finite, connected, and bipartite, with coloring $\chi(h)\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$. Every edge difference has rank two and signature $(1,1)$. Every multiplicity is an integer between $1$ and $1251$. \item Let \[ F(t)=1-\frac{15}{28}t^2+\frac{13}{80}t^4 -\frac{41}{1008}t^6+\frac1{70}t^8. \] There is a nonzero rational Weil class $w$, normalized by complementary matrix entries equal to one, for which \begin{equation}\label{eisenstein-trace-eq:ch} \sum_{hZ,\sigma}M_{h,\sigma}\exp(D_{h,\sigma}) =626\,|H/Z|\,8!F(\theta) +160225344\,|H/Z|\,\frac{49}{41616}\,w. \end{equation} Here $|H/Z|=13436928$. \item For every $B\in\mathcal T$, the weighted diagonal obstruction vector belongs to the image of the incidence map: \[ \bigl(M_{h,\sigma}\,\kappa_B\mathbin{\lrcorner}D_{h,\sigma} \bigr)_{hZ,\sigma} \in\im\left(\bigoplus_e q_e\longrightarrow \bigoplus_{hZ,\sigma}H^2(A,\mathcal O_A)\right). \] The edge coefficients depend linearly on $B$. In the indicated bases they belong to $K$ whenever the coordinates of $B$ belong to $K$. \end{enumerate} A common integral scaling makes the vertices line-bundle classes and preserves the trace conclusion. No full Atiyah-obstruction, deformation, or semiregularity conclusion is included.

statement: [Rational phase transfer]\label{eisenstein-trace-lem:transfer} Let $p(z)=a_{-1}z^{-1}+a_0+a_1z+a_2z^2$ with $a_j$ in a rational vector space. Set \[ B_4=[p(1),p(-1),\operatorname{Re}_i p(i),\operatorname{Im}_i p(i)], \qquad B_6=[p(1),p(-1),\Ree p(\zeta),\Imm p(\zeta)]. \] Then $B_4=B_6T$, where \begin{equation}\label{eisenstein-trace-eq:T} T=\begin{pmatrix} 1&0&-1/2&-1/2\\ 0&1&1/6&-1/6\\ 0&0&4/3&2/3\\ 0&0&0&2 \end{pmatrix}. \end{equation} Both sets of four columns span the rational coefficient span of $p$.

statement: [Products of two point ideals]\label{prop:point-product-spin} Let $X,Y$ be abelian fourfolds, let $p\in X$, $q\in Y$, and let $L,M$ be line bundles. No character obtained from \[ (I_p\otimes L)\boxtimes(I_q\otimes M) \] by Fourier--Mukai equivalences, rational isogeny pullbacks or pushforwards, rational $B$-field transformations and nonzero scalar multiplication remains Hodge on a full polarized Weil domain of signature $(4,4)$.

[A single point secant]\label{prop:single-point-spin} Let $Z$ be an abelian eightfold and let $c\in\Q^\times$. Apply any sequence of the rational Clifford operations above to $1+c[\mathrm{pt}_Z]$, obtaining $z$. If $z$ remains Hodge on a full polarized Weil domain of signature $(4,4)$ with polarization $\theta$, then \[ z\in\Q[\theta]. \] In particular its Weil component is zero.

[All products of point secants]\label{thm:all-point-products} Let $A_1,\ldots,A_s$ be positive-dimensional abelian varieties with $\sum_i\dim A_i=8$. For nonzero rational $r_i,c_i$, put \[ f=\boxtimes_{i=1}^s\bigl(r_i+c_i[\mathrm{pt}_{A_i}]\bigr). \] Apply any sequence of Fourier--Mukai equivalences, rational isogeny pullbacks or pushforwards, rational $B$-field transformations and nonzero scalar multiplication. If the resulting character $z$ is Hodge on a full polarized Weil domain of signature $(4,4)$, then $z\in\Q[\theta]$. Thus its Weil component is zero. In particular no external product of line-bundle twists of point ideals, for any partition of dimension eight, gives the required full-family Weil detector character by these operations.

\label{thm:localized-support} Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ be translates of abelian subvarieties of the same codimension $c$ in a complex abelian variety $A$. Suppose every pairwise intersection has codimension at least two in each component. Let $E$ be a perfect complex whose cohomology sheaves are supported on $ igcup_iZ_i$. Write \[ m_i(E)=\sum_j(-1)^j \operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{A,\eta_i}} \mathcal H^j(E)_{\eta_i} \] for its generic virtual multiplicity at $Z_i$. For a first-order deformation $\kappa\in H^1(A,T_A)$, let $
u_i(\kappa)\in H^1(Z_i,N_{Z_i/A})$ be its normal restriction. If $m_i(E)
e0$ and $
u_i(\kappa)
e0$ for some $i$, then $E$ has no perfect deformation in direction $\kappa$, even with an arbitrary infinitesimal gerbe twist.

\label{lem:mumford-plane} The primitive space $P$ has dimension $27$ and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathrm{HS}}(P)=F$. The rational Hodge classes of codimension two on $A^2$ form the direct sum of the six-dimensional space of divisor products and a two-dimensional space \[ E\simeq F^0:=\ker(\operatorname{Tr}_{F/\Q}:F\longrightarrow\Q). \] The identification is induced by $P\otimes P\simeq\operatorname{End}_{\Q}(P)$ using $Q_2$.

\label{thm:mumford-cubic} For every fixed nonzero rational class $t\in E$, there is a constant $C_t>0$ such that \[ \delta_{\mathrm{exc}}\leq c_t\leq C_t\delta_{\mathrm{exc}}^3. \] The constants may be chosen uniformly on the Hodge-generic fibres of one fixed polarized Mumford family, after a fixed finite cover making $E$ and $t$ global. In particular, one nonzero algebraic exceptional class implies algebraicity of the whole exceptional plane at a Hodge-generic fibre.

\label{lem:mumford-cost} Give a rational cycle $Z=\sum_i r_iZ_i$ the signed cost $|Z|_\Theta=\sum_i|r_i|\deg_\Theta Z_i$. The fixed operators just described change cost $B$ to at most $CB$, with fixed denominators. Composition of two correspondences on $A$ of costs $B_1,B_2$ has a signed representative of cost at most $C'B_1B_2$. The constants depend only on the fixed data and are uniform in the polarized family.

\label{cor:mumford-family} On a fixed connected Mumford Shimura curve, suppose that detectors for its exceptional plane have degrees bounded by one integer $D$ at infinitely many CM points. Then, for every fixed global $t\in E$, the complexity $c_t$ is bounded on every fibre.

[One surface correspondence suffices]\label{thm:mumford-surface} Suppose there is an algebraic cycle \[ Z\in\mathrm{CH}^2(S_\lambda\times C\times C)_{\mathbf Q} \] whose correspondence action has a nonzero component \begin{equation} \gamma:T(S_\lambda)\longrightarrow H^1(C,\mathbf Q)\otimes H^1(C,\mathbf Q). \label{eq:mumford-surface-map} \end{equation} Then the entire exceptional plane $E\subset H^4(A^2,\mathbf Q)$ is algebraic. It is enough to find one effective irreducible surface $Z$ with this property.
[The square class of a dominant graph]\label{prop:mumford-graph-twist} If a dominant rational map $f:C\times C\dashrightarrow S_\lambda$ exists, then $\lambda\in\mathbf Q^\times F^{\times2}$.

[An order-three K3 realization of the Mumford datum] \label{clifford-lem:k3-realization} Let $F$ be a totally real cubic field and let $D/F$ be a quaternion algebra split at precisely one real place and ramified at the other two. Put $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and $E=FK$. Assume that $D\otimes_FE$ and $\operatorname{Cor}_{F/\mathbb Q}D$ are split. The first condition holds, in particular, if $D$ is unramified at every finite place. For every Hodge-generic Mumford fourfold $A$ belonging to this datum there is a projective K3 surface $S$ with a non-symplectic automorphism of order three such that: \begin{enumerate} \item the pair belongs to $\mathcal M_{0,1}$, and $S$ may be chosen in the open locus of smooth models \[ f_2(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)=0,\qquad f_3(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3)+x_4^3=0 \quad\text{in }\mathbb P^4; \] \item $U=T(S)_{\mathbb Q}$ has rank $12$ and is two-dimensional over $E$, with adjoint involution complex conjugation; its $E/F$-Hermitian form has signatures $(1,1),(0,2),(0,2)$ and special unitary group $\operatorname{SL}_1(D)$; \item the Hodge point of $U$ is the prescribed point of the Mumford disk, and $A$ is an isogeny factor of the Kuga--Satake variety associated with $U$. \end{enumerate} Only rational $E$-endomorphisms of $U$ are asserted. No integral $\mathcal O_E$-action or algebraicity of the Kuga--Satake correspondence is part of this assertion.

statement: \label{lem:rational-base-fiber-product} Let $S$ and $X$ be smooth projective complex surfaces, let $R$ be a smooth projective rational surface, and let $p:S\dashrightarrow R$ be dominant.
